subject: Request: Fast-track deterministic telemetry for CapitalEdge pilot
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@capitaledge.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@capitaledge.com
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production pilot telemetry — urgent ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CapitalEdge is ready to move the pilot to production for a portion of our flows (target date Oct 20). Before we switch this on we need deterministic, per-request telemetry so our observability and billing can reconcile end-to-end. Specifically we need: 

- a propagated trace_id on every request/response that appears in traces and logs
- per-request latency and model-selection metadata (which model variant served the request)
- a lightweight per-token latency stub or token-count metric we can use to reconcile cost (doesn't need to be exact per-token timing, but must be deterministic for our billing)

This is blocking our internal compliance and procurement sign-off. We can share a short spec (attached) and procurement has indicated willingness to convert this to a committed pilot contract if Redwood can deliver a scoped implementation for Oct pilot.

Can you let me know if this is something you can prioritize and what the minimum viable scope is?

Cheers,
Karen Liu
Head of Infrastructure
CapitalEdge

Attachments: capitaledge-telemetry-spec.pdf
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production pilot telemetry — urgent ask (CapitalEdge)

Team — forwarding CapitalEdge's ask. Short summary: they need deterministic request-level telemetry (trace id propagation + model metadata + a token-cost-compatible metric) for an Oct 20 pilot. Procurement is willing to convert to a committed pilot (deal id CE-202610) if we can ship a scoped solution. I attached the term sheet we discussed (commercial incentive).

Can Product/Eng review feasibility/ETA? Sales is offering a $250k committed usage for prioritization; CS (Marissa) will run pilot success criteria.

Key questions:
- Minimal implementation that satisfies procurement/compliance?
- Rough ETA and required scope (sidecar/export vs runtime change)?
- Any security/compliance blockers for exporting model-selection metadata?

Appreciate quick responses — procurement is asking for a go/no-go by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: capitaledge-incentive-term-sheet.pdf
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production pilot telemetry — urgent ask (CapitalEdge)

Thanks Priyom — looping Product in.

High-level thoughts from product perspective: the ask splits into three distinct capabilities:

1) Trace-id propagation (headers + logging) — low risk. We already propagate trace ids internally; adding a stable trace_id that surfaces in the public response header and our logs should be feasible as a short project.

2) Model-selection metadata (which model/config served a request) — also straightforward to emit into logs/structured events; need to confirm privacy/security with Security team but should be ok if we don't include prompt content.

3) Deterministic per-token latency/cost metric — this is the trickiest. Our runtime doesn't currently expose token-level timing/costs in a deterministic, export-ready form. Options:
   - Option A (MVP): emit per-request token_count + end-to-end token-generation latency (single metric). Deterministic and fast to add (2 weeks with 1 eng + 1 infra).
   - Option B (Full): per-token latency samples + attribution to internal cost buckets. More accurate but requires infra changes and ~6-8 weeks.

If Sales is offering committed spend, Product can prioritize Option A for the pilot. We need Eng to confirm feasibility and whether sampling could meet CapitalEdge's reconciliation needs.

Questions for Eng:
- What is the minimal surface area to deliver Option A?
- Can we guarantee no PII/leakage in outgoing telemetry?

If everyone agrees, I'll propose a scoped RFC early tomorrow and request 2 sprint slots.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Sr PM, Product — Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production pilot telemetry — urgent ask (CapitalEdge)

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 10:08 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> If Sales is offering committed spend, Product can prioritize Option A for the pilot.

Quick technical take and suggested path:

We can break this into three implementation tracks:

A) Header-level trace_id propagation + logging export — low lift (1 week):
   - Add deterministic trace_id in public response headers and wire into our logging/OTel pipeline.
   - Provide a toggle (customer-level) to enable/disable for privacy.

B) Model-selection metadata emission — low lift (1 week):
   - Emit model_id/model_variant to structured logs and event stream; mask prompt contents.

C) Token-cost-compatible metric:
   - MVP (Option A from Product): token_count + total generation latency per request. This is implementable with minimal runtime change (2 weeks, 1 Eng + 1 Infra). Deterministic for reconciliation because token_count is exact and latency is a single aggregate metric.
   - Full per-token attribution would require changes to kernel telemetry hooks and our cost attribution pipeline (6–8 weeks, blocking other prioritized work).

Recommendation for pilot: implement A + B + MVP C with a deterministic sample key so CapitalEdge can reconcile at 100% for pilot traffic. We can backfill more detailed per-token info later if the account expands.

I will prepare a short implementation note and estimate resources — attaching a quick scope doc. Major risks: increased event volume (cost/ingest), need to ensure telemetry contains no prompt text, and gating by security/privacy review.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Attachments: implementation-scope.md
From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production pilot telemetry — decision and ask

Team — thanks for the quick triage.

Summary & ask:
- CapitalEdge is on board to move forward if we can deliver header trace_id + model metadata + the MVP token metric (token_count + generation_latency) for their Oct 20 pilot.
- Sales is formally committing CE-202610 for $250k committed usage in exchange for prioritization — procurement copied here.
- Product/Eng recommendation (Markus/Irene) to scope A+B+MVP C is acceptable to the customer.

Can Eng confirm availability to take this as a priority for the next sprint cycle and provide a short rollout plan (toggle, security review, ETA for pilot-ready)? If we get a firm commitment from Eng today we can finalize the commercial term sheet with procurement and lock the pilot dates.

I'll set up a 30-min alignment call for later today to walk through the proposed scope and sign-off.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
